cognate: *wérǵom 'deed' as the second member of a 'word and deed' merism: Arm. gorc, Gk ἔργον, Av. (hu-)varəšta- (*wr̥ǵ-to-), OE weorc/OS uuerc/ON verk
drift_or_renewal: the 'word' member is renewed in most branches (Arm. ban, Gk λόγος beside the older ἔπος, Gmc *wurda-); Greek ἔπος and Av. uxta- (both *wekʷ-) keep a cognate 'word' member, so Homer ἔπος/ἔργον ~ Av. hūxta/huuaršta is the fully cognate pair
shared_syntax: coordinated nouns 'words and deeds' (Arm. zbans ew zgorcs, ban ew gorc; Gk ἔργα ... καὶ λόγους; Hom. ἔργον τε ἔπος τε; Av. hūxta- ... huuaršta-; OE wordum ond worcum) as a polar expression for the whole of a person's conduct
context: Movses uses it of the full record of famous men (what they said and did; 'as the man and his deeds, so the words about him'); Thucydides of matching deeds and words; Homer of a hero's total capacity (τελέσαι ἔργον τε ἔπος τε) and of help 'by word or deed'; Avesta of the ethical whole; Beowulf of a retainer's or king's conduct
note: The figure itself is old (Homer, Old/Young Avestan, secular Old English). The Armenian anchor is the weak link: Movses is a Hellenizing author, the Armenian Bible has the same pairing (Luke 24:19), and Christian 'thought, word and deed' (Arm. xorhurd, ban, gorc, frequent in Agathangelos/Gregory) or Iranian humata/hūxta/huuaršta could be the model; Thucydides' λόγος/ἔργον is rhetorical. Low confidence that the slab passages continue rather than reflect it; the cognate deed-word across four branches is what is defended.

search_lead.cognate: Arm. mawrukʻ 'beard' (Movses' form մաւրուս, acc.pl.) ~ Ved. śmáśru- < *smóḱru-
search_lead.argument: In the Vahagn birth song the god has fire for hair, flame for a beard (bocʻ ownēr mawrowsn) and is xartеаš 'blond'; Vahagn is the Armenian reflex of Iranian Vərəθraγna, whose Vedic counterpart epithet vṛtrahán belongs to Indra, the god in the RV whose beard is singled out as hári- 'yellow/golden' (RV 10.23.4) and shaken (10.23.1, 10.26.7 of Pūṣan). Same cognate noun for the dragon-slaying god's beard with a colour/fire attribute; the fire word is renewed. Generic description of a beard is possible and Armenian may draw on Iranian imagery, so this is a lead, not a claim.
